tldr: For a fixed binary roster, the critical growing-menu precision deficit has the unique evaluated limit \(J(n,m)\to\Lambda(r)\) when \(m/n^{1/4}\to r>0\). Its terminating deterministic error certificate and original-record procedures are matched by complete-table priors fixed before assignment, against every legal outcome-independent design and full-record rule. Defining \(a_{\mathrm{aff}}(n)=n^{-1}-(1+\sqrt n)^{-2}\), the unrestricted relative improvement satisfies \(d(n,m)/a_{\mathrm{aff}}(n)\to\Lambda(r)/2\), uniformly on compact positive critical-ratio intervals. This compares deficits with the credited scalar-affine signed-score benchmark, rather than asserting its optimality among all affine full-record rules. After the critical limit, the relative-gain endpoints are \((C_A/2)r^{-2/3}\{1+O_c(e^{-c/r^2})\}\) and \(\sqrt2+1/(24r^2)+O(r^{-4})\).
